Attachment chip

One file or image attached to a prompt: its kind as an icon, its name, its size in words and a button that removes it.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • Above or below a composer, for each file or image the reader attached to the prompt they are writing.
  • While an attachment uploads, and when its upload fails.

When not to use it

  • For a reference to a file in the repository, a page or a commit. Use a source chip, which is a link.
  • For a file listed in a sent message or a changed-files list. Use a dense list.
  • For a status. Use a badge.
  • For choosing the file. Use the browser's file input, labelled as a field.

Variants

file
The file icon, for anything that is not an image.
image
The image icon, with a ds-visually-hidden span reading Image before the name, so the kind is not the icon alone.

Accessibility

  • Each chip is an li with the class ds-attachment-chip, in a ul with an aria-label such as Attachments. Lay the ul out with ds-cluster ds-gap-md: the 12px gap keeps the remove buttons' 44px pointer targets on two rows from overlapping.
  • Write the whole file name as text, split into ds-attachment-chip__start and ds-attachment-chip__end with no white space between the spans. The end part is the last few characters with the extension. The stylesheet cuts the middle from view only, so a screen reader still reads the whole name.
  • Write the size with its unit, such as 48 KB or 2.1 MB.
  • The remove control is a button element with type="button" and the class ds-attachment-chip__remove, holding the x icon with aria-hidden="true" and a ds-visually-hidden span that names the file: Remove session-trace.log. It is drawn 24px square and its pointer target is 44px each way.
  • While the file uploads, set aria-busy="true" on the li and add a native progress element with the class ds-attachment-chip__progress as its last child, with value and max set from the upload and an aria-label such as Uploading session-trace.log. Leave value off until the first figure arrives. Put the percentage and the size in ds-attachment-chip__size, and name the button Cancel the upload of and the file.
  • When the upload fails, remove aria-busy and the progress element and add a p with the class ds-attachment-chip__error and role="alert" as the last child. It says what happened and what to do, such as Not attached: files can be up to 10 MB. Remove it and attach a smaller file. Its icon and the chip's outline are drawn by the stylesheet.
  • While the prompt is being sent, set the disabled attribute on each remove button.
  • After a chip is removed, move focus to the next chip's remove button, or to the composer when none is left.
  • Tab reaches each remove button. Enter and Space activate it. The component needs no script of its own: the app sets aria-busy, the progress value, the text and the disabled attribute.
